## Fix round 2 acceptance tests: written. Tier L ran, with 4 expected failures; Tier H not run

The 4 Tier L failures are all C-FR2.3 Terraform checks. They fail because the builder has not changed `infra/` yet; they are not test faults. Nothing is committed. I wrote only under `*/test-acceptance/**` and the run dir, and did not read spec.md or implementation.md.

### New files (in `C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build/api/test-acceptance/`)

- **`hardening-id-case.acc.test.ts`** (C-FR2.1, Tier H)
  - **FR2-C01:** E edits an invoice via `PUT /dd/invoices/{UPPER-CASE id}`, then F edits it later. E is neither the creator nor the last editor. M2 audits it. E's approve and reject both get 403 `four_eyes_required` with basis `dd_invoice_editor`, including through an upper-case approve URL. A neutral reviewer then approves with 200.
  - **FR2-C02:** `POST /claims/{UPPER-CASE id}/analyze`, then the author of an influencing label is refused (403, basis `label_author`) through both lower- and upper-case URLs. The approval queue shows the same basis. M1 then approves with 200.
  - **FR2-C03:** owner SQL finds no audit row with `target_id <> lower(target_id)`. Ids in metadata are lower case, the packet `claimId` is lower case, and no response echoes the upper- or mixed-case id.
  - **FR2-C04:** upper- and mixed-case GETs of the invoice, claim, packet and charge-lines return the same body as the lower-case GET.
- **`hardening-label-cap.acc.test.ts`** (C-FR2.2, Tier H)
  - **FR2-L01, exactly 50 labels:** the truncation flag is absent or false, the ids match, in-list authors are refused, and the author of a label that matches no charge line approves with 200.
  - **FR2-L02, 60 labels:** `learnedLabelIds` holds the first 50 and the flag is true. RT, who wrote only labels 51 to 60, is refused on approve and reject with basis `label_author`.
  - **FR2-L03:** the database guard refuses RT's approval insert (as `freight_app`) with P0001 `four_eyes_required`.
  - **FR2-L04:** a neutral reviewer approves with 200.
- **`hardening-infra-fr2.acc.test.ts`** (C-FR2.3, Tier L), checks FR2-I01 to I06 over `infra/*.tf` and `infra/README.md`:
  - **(a)** the origin-verify rule either forwards only on a `random_password` value (no committed literal, also through locals) or answers a fixed 403. If `random_password` is used, the random provider must be declared and pinned. The README deploy gate must say a request with a placeholder value gets 403.
  - **(b)** no whole-origin or `all` `ignore_changes` unless a `check {}` block covers origin `domain_name` and `origin_protocol_policy`. Without that ignore, the origin header must not be a literal.
  - **(c)** either the managed `Managed-AllViewerExceptHostHeader` policy, or the custom policy plus `host_header [var.app_domain]` and a certificate precondition. The choice must be written in the README.
  - A test-only `FR2_INFRA_DIR` override (never set in CI) lets the checks run on a copy of `infra/`. On scratch copies, both allowed designs pass 6/6, and each of the two negative variants fails exactly the intended check.
  - `terraform fmt/validate` stays in the existing HP-C07 case, which declares a skip when the binary is missing.

### Changes to existing tests (each forced by the amendment; nothing loosened)

- **`helpers/analysis.ts`:** new `baseMeta()` for the 7 exact `claim.analyzed` pins in `analysis`, `analysis-bulk`, `charge-analysis`, `fuel-api` and `hardening-failed`. It now fails if `learnedLabelIdsTruncated` is true and drops a false value, since the spec allows "absent or false".
- **`hardening-static` HP-C07:** removed three assertions (the custom-policy check, the "has ignore_changes" check, and "the rule forwards", now "a rule matches on x-origin-verify"). Their amended versions are FR2-I02, I05 and I06.
- **Migration pins (HD-S01, `dd-static`, `fuel-static`):** they now allow exactly one more folder, `20261019000000_hardening_fr2`, which the builder added.
  - `20261018000000_hardening` is pinned to its committed sha (cd596c3, `41b7a7df...`).
  - A new check, FR2-S01, whitelists the new migration's statements: only `CREATE OR REPLACE` of the two existing guard functions (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path) plus their REVOKE. It passes now.
